paragraphs.text: Cell-aware Jupyter notebook tools for DSH agents
# dsh-plugin-notebook-tools

Cell-aware Jupyter notebook tools for DSH agents. A zero-dependency Node ESM
plugin that ports the O

penClaw `notebook-tools` plugin (9 tools) onto the DSH
host.

The core `read` / `write` / `edit` tools treat `.ipynb` files as opaque JSON,
which is error-prone,

token-hungry, and easy to corrupt. This plugin provides a
structured, cell-aware API instead: stable

cell ids, output-aware truncation,
stale-edit guards, and format-preserving atomic writes.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin` forwards to the pnpm bundled with DSH, and `--profile` is
required. The `--config.minim

umReleaseAge=0` override is needed while the
target profile's *existing* lockfile entries are newer

than pnpm's default
`minimumReleaseAge` cutoff (pnpm 11.7.0 enforces that default even when the
prof

ile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists the same offenders under
`minimumReleaseAgeExclude`). Without it y

ou get
`ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` naming packages you did not touch.

On success the package is appended to **both** `dependencies` and
`dsh.profile.bundles` in `<DSH_HOM

E>\profiles\<profile>\package.json` — no
manual edit needed. A failed run can still leave a link in

`node_modules`, so
treat the `package.json` entry, not `node_modules`, as proof.

The plugin ships a `cordis.patch.yml` that inserts it under the id
`notebook-tools`. DSH composes th

at row at boot, so **restart the DSH app** for
the tools to appear in an already-running session.

No dependencies are installed: `pnpm install` is unnecessary, and the package
imports only `node:` b

dencies are installed: `pnpm install` is unnecessary, and the package
imports only `node:` builtins.

e tools, which of them can mutate a notebook, and how

unlike the plugin it
self, which is composed at boot.
## Tools
| Tool | Writes | Purpose |

| `notebook_create` | yes | Create a notebook from structured cells |
| `notebook_read` | no | Struc

tured read, optionally with outputs |
| `notebook_list_cells` | no | Cheap index: id, type, preview,

counts |
| `notebook_search` | no | Find cells by text or regex |
| `notebook_validate` | no | Vali

date structure and report facts |
| `notebook_edit_cell` | yes | Replace a cell's source / type |
|

`notebook_insert_cell` | yes | Insert a new cell at a position |
| `notebook_delete_cell` | yes | De

lete a cell by id or index |
| `notebook_clear_outputs` | yes | Clear outputs (all or one cell) |
## Guarantees

- **Writes preserve the file's own formatting.** The plugin probes the layout a
notebook already use

s — JSON indent (0/1/2/4), CRLF vs LF, trailing newline —
and writes it back unchanged, so a noteboo

k produced by JupyterLab,
`nbformat.writes`, or a text editor is not reformatted. A cell whose `sour

ce`
is a plain string stays a string, and keys that were absent (`outputs`,
`execution_count`, `meta

data`) are not invented. Read-then-write with no edit
is byte-identical. Not preserved: tab indentat

ion, `\uXXXX`-escaped non-ASCII
(Python's `ensure_ascii=True`), and more than one trailing newline.

- **Atomic saves.** Mutations serialize to a sibling temp file
(`.‹basename›.tmp-‹pid›-‹counter›-‹ra

ndom›`) in the same directory, `fsync` it,
then `rename` over the target. A killed process can never

leave a half-written
notebook, and no temp file ever lands in the system temp directory.
- **Valida

tion before every write.** A notebook that fails the deep audit — cell
ids outside `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1

,64}$` or duplicated, non-object `metadata`,
non-array `outputs`, non-string `source` elements — is

refused by the writers
and reported by `notebook_validate`, instead of being silently rewritten.
- *

*Cell ids over indexes.** `notebook_read`, `notebook_list_cells`, and
`notebook_search` always retur

n an `id`. A notebook too old to store ids
(nbformat < 4.5) gets ids derived from `sha256("v1|<ordin

al>|<source>")`, so
the same cell keeps the same id across loads and processes; the derived id is
pe

rsisted only once the file's format supports ids. `nbformat_minor` is never
bumped. Indexes shift af

ter every insert/delete — prefer ids.
- **Editing a code cell clears `outputs` and `execution_count`

,** and the
response text says so.
- **Three stale-edit guards on every mutating tool.** `expected_f

ile_sha256`
catches any change to the bytes on disk — including a rewrite inside the same
millisecon

d, which `expected_file_mtime_ms` cannot see; `expected_source_sha256`
catches a change to the one c

ell an operation depends on (the anchor cell for
an insert, the target cell for an edit, delete, or

clear); the mtime check is
[该节后续省略]

read` or `notebook_list_cells`, `source_sha256` only from
`notebook_read`.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Tests use `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` and require Node >= 22 (verified
on Node 24).
## Releasing

Releases are one command, run from a clean `main` that already contains the
version bump:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

It refuses to run unless `CHANGELOG.md` carries a non-empty `## [<version>]`
section and a `[<versio

n>]:` link reference for the version in `package.json`,
the working tree is clean, and HEAD is the c

ommit that carries the bump. Then it
runs `node --test`, pushes the release branch, creates the anno

tated tag
`v<version>`, pushes it, and
creates the GitHub Release: the tag annotation is the release

title and the
CHANGELOG section is its body. Credentials come from `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN`,
fal

ling back to the stored `git credential` for `github.com` (nothing is ever
printed); the GitHub CLI

stored `git credential` for `github.com` (nothing is ever
printed); the GitHub CLI is not required.

Other flags: `--dry-run` (print the plan, change nothing), `--skip-tests`,
`--branch <name>` (defaul
t `main`), `--remote <name>` (default `origin`).
